audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flags it directly: Akshan wins 55.01% over 1705 games but the chart hands LeBlanc five of seven stages. On top of that, phases[N].side reads 'Skill' on all seven rows while win[N] reads Akshan/LeBlanc — the same row rendering two answers.
audit.why: A 55% win rate cannot sit under a chart that says the enemy owns levels 2 through first item. The grounded correction is the early rows: Akshan's Avengerang is 850 and his autos out-range LeBlanc's Sigil of Malice at 700, so before Mimic exists at 6 she has to step inside his range to start anything, and her combo cannot burst through the three-hit passive shield. Levels 4-5 through first item stay hers — that is where Mimic doubles the rotation.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Akshan / Akshan / Akshan / LeBlanc / LeBlanc / LeBlanc / Akshan across both layers, proposed as one atomic group.
sources: brief kits (Akshan Q 850, LeBlanc Q 700, R 45/35/25)

audit.why: Spike ordering is right: her window is Mimic at 6 into first item; Akshan reclaims late with Comeuppance against her overextensions. spikes[] entry count is 4 and unchanged.

audit.whatIsWrong: Ethereal Chains — LeBlanc's only lockdown and the ability that actually kills Akshan — is not mentioned anywhere on the page. Neither is Mirror Image.
audit.why: Ethereal Chains is 925 range, longer than Akshan's 850 Q, and it shackles first: the root and the extra damage only land if the target is still tethered 1.5 seconds later. Heroic Swing or a wall breaking that leash inside 1.5s cancels the root outright — that is the decisive interaction of the matchup and every page field talks about Distortion instead. It also reveals stealth, so it answers Akshan's W camouflage. Mirror Image: under 40% health she goes invisible for 1 second and leaves a damage-less clone for up to 8 seconds — relevant every time Akshan chips her toward an execute.
audit.corrected: Chains written into early, breakdown.cooldowns, wants.foe[0] and wants.you[1] with its range and its 1.5-second window; Mirror Image's 40% threshold and clone added to early.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns named only Distortion and gave no numbers.
audit.why: Distortion is 15s at rank 1 with a 4-second return window; Ethereal Chains is 14s at 925; Sigil of Malice is a flat 6s that refunds its mana and part of its cooldown if either half secures the kill — so 'her Q is down' is not a safe assumption after she finishes a minion with it.
audit.corrected: All three cooldowns written in with the Sigil refund noted.
sources: brief enemyKit cooldowns and Q text

audit.why: No rank language in Common Mistakes or anywhere in breakdown.late.

edits.before: LeBlanc's poke-and-blink combo starts outpacing your trades once she can safely engage
edits.after: Her Sigil reaches 700 and yours reaches 850 — she cannot trade without stepping in

edits.before: Her burst window widens further as she gets more consistent access to her full combo
edits.after: Without Mimic at 6, her combo cannot burst through your three-hit passive shield

edits.before: LeBlanc's kit is built entirely around safe poke and burst — she lands Sigil of Malice from range then follows with Distortion to either engage or escape, and your only reliable answer early is patience. Don't trade into her W cooldown blind; wait for her to commit W before pressuring, and use E Heroic Swing reactively to dodge her Q rather than proactively. This phase belongs to her more than you, so prioritize farm safety over aggression.
edits.after: LeBlanc pokes with Sigil of Malice (Q) at 700 while your boomerang reaches 850, so she has to step inside your range to start anything. The real threat is Ethereal Chains (E) at 925: it shackles first and only roots if you are still tethered 1.5 seconds later, so break the leash with Heroic Swing or a wall and the root never happens. Under 40 percent health her passive turns her invisible for a second and leaves a clone — do not chase the wrong one.

edits.before: Save E Heroic Swing to dodge her Q Sigil rather than for aggression
edits.after: Save Heroic Swing to break Ethereal Chains inside its 1.5 seconds

edits.before: Land Q Sigil of Malice then combo with W-Q for burst damage
edits.after: Land Ethereal Chains at 925 and hold you 1.5s for the root

edits.before: - LeBlanc Distortion: matchup-defining — Dash with a four-second return window — punish the return spot, and remember she is broke after it. Step up only on its downtime. - Budget E Heroic Swing for emergencies and the R for opportunities — never swap them.
edits.after: - LeBlanc Distortion: matchup-defining — 15s at rank 1 with a 4-second return; punish the return spot, she is broke after it. - Ethereal Chains is 14s and 925 range — break the leash inside 1.5s or eat the root. - Sigil of Malice is a flat 6s and refunds on a kill.

edits.before: LeBlanc wins by landing Distortion, denying your pattern, and front-loading the violence while your kit is still stretching.
edits.after: LeBlanc wins by chaining you at 925, detonating a Sigil, and Mimicking the whole rotation before your shield ticks.

notes: The packet's own defect line was correct and I acted on it: a 55.01% win rate under a chart giving LeBlanc 5 of 7 stages is incoherent. I moved only the rows I could ground in the kits (levels 2 and 3, on the 850-vs-700 range gap and the absence of Mimic before 6) and left her the 4-5 / level 6 / first-item block. All seven phases[N].side values also read 'Skill' against a populated win[N], so the whole chart went in as one atomic group with the two win[] flips paired. Biggest content gap: Ethereal Chains was absent from the entire page despite being her only lockdown and outranging Akshan's Q — its 1.5-second shackle-before-root window is the single most actionable fact in this matchup and is now in four fields. UNVERIFIED, left alone: the brief's missingInteractions claims Heroic Swing 'shuts off LeBlanc's Distortion'. Akshan's E carries a 'terrain' flag in the kit file, but Riot's description says he fires a hook INTO terrain and swings — it does not create terrain, so I did not assert that his E denies her dash. That flag looks like a tooltip-parse misfire and I treated it as such. Also unverified and therefore unwritten: whether Mirror Image's clone can body-block Comeuppance's bullets (R hits 'the first champion... hit').
